name: P. S. Bemis
role: New Yorker who cowboyed on the Little Missouri
bio: P. S. "Tap" Bemis of New York, lately of Ransom County, joined the round-up at Medora in September 1885 to learn the cattle business. After more than a year cowpunching on the river, he left in September 1886 to run a wagon for an Arizona outfit owned by New York friends.

P. S. Bemis, of New York, lately of Ransom county, Dakota, came to Medora last Saturday and has joined the round-up. He intends getting a practical insight into the cattle business…
J. A. VanEeghen and "Tap" Bemis went to Miles last week. The latter has returned and "Van" is still in Montana's cow-town.
P. S. Bemis who has been "cow-punching" on the river for over a year, will start Sunday for Arizona. He will run a wagon in a large outfit there owned by some of his New York friend…
